newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to publish National a/c public deficit - Rato.
newsitem.headline: Spain to publish National a/c public deficit - Rato.

text.p: Spain' Economy Ministry will soon begin to publish monthly data on the central government public deficit on a national account basis, Economy Ministry Rodrigo Rato said on Wednesday at an economic conference in Spain.

The central government public deficit an a national account basis is the one considered relevant for the Maastricht Treaty criteria. It takes into account accrued revenues and expenditures for a given period.
So far the Spanish government has published only central government deficit on a cash basis, which registers actual money movements during a given month.
On November 18, Spain said its October cash deficit was 55.2 billion pesetas and Budget Secretary Jose Folgado explained the unexpectedly wide deficit with delayed payments from previous years.
Without these delayed payments, he said, the October central government would have been a surplus of 84.9 billion pesetas.
In the first 10 months, the central government's accumulated deficit on a cash basis was 2.236 billion pesetas.
Meanwhile, the deficit on a national account basis in the first 10 months of 1996 was at 1.78 billion pesetas, or 2.4 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), according to Folgado.

The 1996 government target is a central government deficit of 3.5 percent over GDP and of 4.4 percent for the public administration. The Maastricht's Treaty requires a country to have a public administration deficit of no more than three percent over GDP in 1997.
